newsitem.title: USA: Exxon joins LNG effort to use Yemen natgas.
newsitem.headline: Exxon joins LNG effort to use Yemen natgas.

text.p: Exxon Corp said it has agreed to take a 14.5 percent interest in a liquified natural gas venture to market natural gas reserves it found in Yemen.

Under agreements the company's Exxon Yemen LNG Co Ltd affiliate reached of with the Republic of Yemen and others, the natural gas will be developed for the local market, and the sale and export of LNG to foreign markets.
When completed, the project will export 5.3 million metric tonnes per year of LNG over 25 years, Exxon said.
Exxon Yemen LNG holds a 14.5 percent interest in the LNG project.
Other members of the LNG venture are Total SA, 36 percent; the Republic of Yemen, 26 percent; Yemen Hunt LNG Co LLC, 15.1 percent; and Yukong Ltd, 8.4 percent.

In a statement Sunday, Total put the value of the project at $5 billion. Exxon spokesman Ed Burwell said the group expects to spend $2.5 billion on shore and suggested the rest must be for LNG tankers.

The natural gas reserves of some 10 trillion cubic feet required for the project were discovered in the Marib Production Sharing Agreement Area by Yemen Exploration & Production Co, a partnership of Hunt Oil and Exxon, it said.

The partnership will continue to operate the Marib reserves, and conduct natural gas operations for a new upstream venture, through expiration of the production sharing agreement, Exxon said. Thereafter, a new operating company, formed by Yemen Exploration & Production Co, Yemen LNG Co, and the Republic of Yemen, will assume operations.
Exxon said its interest in the natural gas operations is about 14.8 percent.
The project will build 320 kilometers of pipelines to connect these reserves with the planned LNG plant, Total said.
Yemen's petroleum minister said the proposed plant could be enlarged to increase exports by 300,000 tonnes a year.
He said the project is talking to LNG importers in Turkey, Japan and Korea.

Exxon said Yemen LNG Co, formed when Total first proposed the LNG venture, will be reconstituted by the new partners to manage the design, construction and operation of the LNG plant and natural gas pipelines; conduct all commercial activities; and provide oversight of the upstream field operations.

The agreements governing the project take effect with the reconstitution of Yemen LNG Co after the passage of the primary agreements by the Yemeni Parliament and signing of the agreements into law by the President of Yemen.

Rex W. Tillerson, president of Exxon Yemen Inc, parent company of Exxon Yemen LNG, stated, "We are pleased that the long process of constructing these very complex agreements among the parties is complete and we look forward to the Yemen Parliament's positive consideration of the two laws.
